OIML certificates typically have format like "R49/2003-DE1-07.02" where R49 is the recommendation, 2003 is the year of the recommendation edition, DE1 is the issuing authority code (PTB Germany), 07.02 is the certificate sequence number (year 07, number 02).

Register form: "R049/2003-DE1-2007.02" — this looks like a canonicalized form: R049, 2003 edition, DE1 issuer, 2007.02 (year 2007, cert 02). So the certificate number on the document is "R49-1/2003-DE1-07.02" which includes the part number -1.

The register canonical form drops the part suffix and zero-pads 49 to 049, and expands 07 to 2007. Per the rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." The register form is the database's canonical form; the difference is formatting (zero padding, expansion of year). The "-1" part suffix... Hmm, is that a genuine difference or a formatting nuance?
